# Cairn v0.1.0-alpha.9

Publication requires a separate evidence commit whose report names this exact
candidate SHA and has no required `NOT RUN` or `FAIL` gates. The source commit's
report is an intentionally incomplete template.

## Deployment

The supported Compose topology serves web at `/` and API at `/api` through one
public proxy port. PostgreSQL, the server API, and web process remain private to the
Compose network. Set `CAIRN_PORT`, `CAIRN_WEB_ORIGIN`, a released
`CAIRN_VERSION`, and administrator bootstrap values in `deploy/.env`; terminate TLS
before the public proxy port. Split-origin deployments are opt-in: set
`CAIRN_API_ORIGIN` and the server's exact `CAIRN_WEB_ORIGIN`, then test the allowed
origin and a denied unrelated origin.

Bootstrap values create an administrator only for a fresh database or one with no
administrator. They do not replace a password changed in web. Back up PostgreSQL
before upgrade. Upgrade server first, install `cairn` and `cairnd` from the same
archive, then rerun `cairn setup` only to repair Cairn-owned integration resources.
Removal is manual: remove only resources named by the last setup report.

## Support and proof

Primary native journeys are Claude Code and Codex. Generic MCP is manual; OpenCode
declined delivery remains a documented capability limit. macOS arm64, Linux arm64 and
x86_64, and Windows x86_64 require installed-artifact evidence. Intel macOS archive
is built but unverified unless this candidate records a native run.

Candidate evidence must include strict PostgreSQL, web contract/type/build, browser
setup, image digest, archive/install, integration ownership, restart, and compaction
for this exact source SHA. The publish workflow then checks downloadable archives
and published image tags.
